title: Give the playlist's failures the answers clients need

blocks.text: A party playlist service lets guests add tracks from their phones. The host can lock the playlist while the DJ reorders it, and the venue's screens get a view that only displays it. Every service of the company answers failures through the same handler, `Playlist.Api.status`, which nobody on your team may change.

Guests complain: the app tells them "server error" when they ask for a track that isn't there, and tells them their request is malformed when they add a song during a reorder, so they never try again.

In `src/main/java/practice/Playlist.java`, finish the three methods that create the exception for each failure, and decide what `NoSuchTrackException` extends. The mobile app catches `NoSuchTrackException` by name, so it stays. The client should learn from the status whether to fix its request, try again later, or stop trying. About four lines in total.

cases.says: a missing position throws NoSuchTrackException carrying the position asked
a locked playlist refuses new tracks and accepts them again once unlocked
the screen view displays the playlist and refuses to add to it
a position the playlist doesn't have, at either end, is answered 400 by the existing handler
a track added while the playlist is locked is answered 409, not as a bad request
an add through the display-only view is answered 405, an operation the object never supports

origin.section: Throw IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException or UnsupportedOperationException When They Already Mean the Error

concepts: IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException and UnsupportedOperationException are already mapped by existing handlers; a home-grown RuntimeException falls through to the fallback, while a subclass of the standard one keeps its meaning.
